The routed water enters every cell's water access downstream of any runoff and a month the land waters — the floodplain, the river, the lake, the routed stream — now counts toward a crop's season, so the static farmed capacity is higher wherever the land is watered (the density ordering's river cells 17.8 → 20.5 persons/km², its rainfed cells 9.8 → 11.6) and the same saturating curve, with no famine variance or mortality, reaches a higher ceiling sooner. Measured 1.438 km/yr Balkans → Rhine on the dev solve arm against the band's 1.3 (Pinhasi, Fort & Ammerman 2005, 0.6–1.3); 1.420 after W12 §1, 1.077 before it. The corrected hop share is not a tuning: a hop of mean square ⟨d²⟩ delivers s·⟨d²⟩/4 of diffusivity, so the share that delivers D is 4·D·dt/⟨d²⟩ and not D·dt/area. The SAME constants measured 0.670 km/yr at the shipped grid after §1 — inside the band for the first time. Identical physics, two grids: the 167 km reference lattice moves a share of a whole cell's people 167 km in a single hop, so its pulled front outruns the continuum 2·√(r·D) the constants name, where the 42 km shipped lattice does not. W13 adds 0.018 km/yr at dev (a wetter Danube corridor carries a slightly denser front). A dev-raster row measured against the grid that ships (third cardinal rule); recorded, not dialed.

Measured −3106 vs latest −5000 (−4200 with the grace) on the dev solve arm — LATE, where every other reached row is early or on time. −3148 after W12 §1, whose corrected share is what first moved it; W13 (the routed water and the watered month) advanced it 42 years and no more, although the Luxor cell's wheat capacity at full technique rises 0.91 → 3.11 persons/km² at the shipped grid under W13 (the valley's winter now counts toward wheat's season, 5 → 8 months). The valley is farmed by sorghum from the Sudan, not by Levantine wheat (see staple:nile:solve:dev), so it is the sorghum route down the valley that sets the date, and sorghum's own belt lights at −6095. WHY a larger share should delay this one arrival is not isolated. The standing candidate is dilution: a firing moves about 2.3× the pre-§1 share out of each cell, and along a corridor one or two cells wide flanked by desert the leading edge thins faster than it accumulates the density adoption needs — which would make the Nile the first place the anisotropic flux of W12 §4 is visible. Recorded as the open question it is, not dialed.

Measured −2027 vs latest −3500 (−2700 with the grace) on the target solve arm. This row is NEW: before W12 §2 the Indus was reached at −3155, inside the window with the grace (see the pre-§2 reason of arrival:ganges:solve:target). §2 moved every European row EARLIER (Balkans −5654 → −6024, central Europe −3722 → −4683, Rhine −2980 → −4161) and this one 1,128 years LATER, on the same wheat front from the same hearth (36.5°N 37.1°E, −7992). Great-circle from that hearth to each box centre, the legs run at 0.73–0.80 km/yr northwest (Balkans, central Europe, Rhine) and 0.54 east to the Indus, 0.66 before §2. Decided by the per-cell arrival raster (QUESTIONS #64, run on request): it is the Iranian plateau's CAPACITY, not the isotropic split. The eastward leg runs at 0.99–1.06 km/yr for its first 500 km and at 0.85–1.17 on the Indus side, but the rings 1,500–2,000 km from the hearth — median static wheat capacity 0.18–0.20 persons/km², wheat fit 0.06 — cross at 0.16–0.30 km/yr, and that 750 km patch costs ~2,400 years, more than this whole miss. The patch is dry in the substrate because the water that farmed the real piedmont sites (Jeitun, Sang-e Chakhmaq, Mehrgarh, Tepe Yahya: mountain runoff onto alluvial fans) is not represented: their annual moisture reads the quantile map's 0.02 floor, their water access 0.02 with river magnitude 0 within ±125 km, so capacity is starved at both the fertility and the fit — a missing mechanism (DECISIONS P17, routed catchment runoff as water access), not a rate to dial, and not to be reached by lifting the floor. The anisotropy test on the same raster shows no east–west penalty at 30–60°N, so §4/P16 does not buy this row. Why §2 moved it 1,128 years later remains unexplained (no pre-§2 raster). Recorded, not dialed. W13 (2026-09-05) built P17, the routed water, and the watered month; measured on the substrate at this grid without history, the plateau sites barely move (Jeitun 0.02 → 0.07, Mehrgarh 0.02 → 0.12, Sang-e Chakhmaq unchanged) because their catchments hold only the runoff floor in the 1.9° table (DECISIONS P18), while the lower Indus gains wheat outright (Mohenjo-daro 4 → 7 months, capacity 0 → 11.4 persons/km²). This row has NOT been re-measured since W13: the shipped-grid solve arm is v2-long, on request (QUESTIONS #65).

A dev-raster row measured against the grid that ships; recorded, not dialed.

The Nile farms sorghum, not wheat, at 1 CE on the dev solve arm: sorghum spreads down the Nile from the Sudan and out-yields wheat there under the crop bells (Egypt's annual warmth sits at wheat's tolerance edge and inside sorghum's), so switching hands the valley to sorghum. The real Nile grew emmer and barley as winter crops on the flood, a season the annual bells do not carry; a data finding on the bells, recorded.

Recorded; the fix is P10 for the seeds' timing and the maize bell's early tolerance (data).

W13 (the routed water, P17, and the watered month) is the only simulation change since the manifest was last measured against this arm (5bd76356, 2026-09-05). The watered month raises millet's fit on the Yangtze's floodplain cells, so the stand there is richer and its clock crosses the lag first, and the standing account of the Hebei hearth is W7's pre-emption: the Yangtze hearth's spread reaches it before its own clock fires. That the box's earliest ignition sits on the Yangtze is the same box-versus-range question as the W9 data item; the steppe, Korean and Kazakh millet ignitions of hearth-outside:millet:solve:dev no longer fire for the same reason. Recorded, not dialed.
